plan.says: Z.ai: not "for general-purpose API access or any scenarios outside such tools, including but not limited to directly invoking model APIs from your own applications, bots": only inside the coding tools it names (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex and Hermes among them).

presets.note: Z.ai's GLM Coding Plan, with the plan's own key (Z.ai keeps plan keys apart from its API keys; the ordinary API is the zai preset). In mainland China: --base-url https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/coding/paas/v4.

plan.name: Kimi Code
plan.says: Kimi: "for interactive use only" (scripted batch runs are named as beyond normal use), and a tool must call as itself, never under another's name.

presets.note: Moonshot's Kimi Code membership, with a key from the Kimi Code console (the pay-as-you-go platform is the moonshot preset; their keys don't work on each other). In mainland China: --base-url https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1.

plan.name: Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan
plan.says: Alibaba: only in coding tools (Claude Code, Qoder, OpenClaw and the like); calls from automation scripts, an application's backend or any non-interactive batch use are forbidden, and may get the key banned.

presets.note: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio's (Bailian's) Coding Plan, with the plan's own sk-sp- key. Outside mainland China the plan has its own address: pass the one your console shows with --base-url.

plan.name: OpenCode Go
plan.says: OpenCode: "designed for OpenCode and other coding agents that send similar traffic", each sending its own User-Agent.

presets.note: Cloudflare AI Gateway's OpenAI-compatible endpoint: --base-url https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/<account id>/<gateway id>/compat. The key is the gateway's token; the providers' own keys stay stored in Cloudflare. Models are named <provider>/<model>, e.g. deepseek/deepseek-chat.
Verda's OpenAI-compatible endpoint is shown in your Verda console; pass it with --base-url
